title: Course files, links and media: ideas from other products
intro: This page gathers ideas for the Files, links and media step inside Courses in Essentials 2.0. It shows how instructors collect, organise, reuse and control course materials, and how learners use them. Sending and distribution belong to sub-module 09. Recording production and reports belong to sub-module 08. The examples come from the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero.

questions.title: Are upload, link and embed handled in one place, or as separate features?
questions.answer: Use one entry point where the instructor is already working, then make the material type and source clear. Podia groups files and embeds under 'New lesson'. Teachable opens an 'Add content' list, then a PDF chooser for device, cloud and URL sources. One shared start menu does not mean one single uploader for every type. Dropbox Dash shows a reusable picker for chat sources, not for course attachments.

questions.title: How is material organised: a flat list, folders, or sections tied to the course?
questions.answer: Course structure and file storage solve different jobs. Kajabi nests lessons inside modules and offers submodules. Teachable shows ordered sections with a short content summary on each lesson. Skillshare uses a flat lesson list plus a resource tab. SuperHi keeps downloads separate from videos. Gumroad is the opposite case: one freeform document instead of visible module rows. For Essentials, try a short course-section structure before adding a separate folder tree.

questions.title: Can materials be reused across courses from a central library, or only inside one course?
questions.answer: Canva shows reuse from a library into a course: choose a design from Projects, then 'Copy to course' or 'Move' it. Dropbox is a similar idea from a file product: a central All files area. Podia and Teachable show adding material inside one course. None of the screenshots show one live file shared across several courses, edits passing through, or pinned versions. Uploading inside a course does not prove materials are locked to that course. Essentials needs clear copy or reference behaviour, and a way to see where a file is used.

questions.title: Can learners preview and play media without leaving the course?
questions.answer: Keep the lesson or library context on screen while someone watches or reads. Coursera plays video in the lesson with study tools and next-item navigation. Dropbox Dash opens a quick look, then a side preview pane. Teachable shows a PDF in the instructor editor; that does not prove learners get the same preview. Skillshare keeps video in the lesson but sends course files to another tab.

questions.title: How do visibility controls for draft, scheduled and per-group access appear on screen?
questions.answer: Treat publish, timed release and who can see the item as separate questions. Teachable pairs a per-lesson 'Publish' control with section-level drip (release delayed after enrollment or on a date). Squarespace keeps Draft, Published and Scheduled labels on screen. Kajabi shows a simpler Draft or Published choice. On Podia, the 'Hidden' label goes away once an item is visible, so there is no lasting visible label. None of these screenshots show visibility limited to a learner group.

questions.title: Does the learner view mirror the instructor-side structure?
questions.answer: No matched pair of screenshots shows a learner view that mirrors its instructor editor. Coursera gives learners a separate Resources branch beside course modules. Skillshare ties project downloads to lessons through references in a separate tab. Udemy shows learner downloads. Teachable shows only the instructor side: sectioned lessons and an attached document. Treat matching structures and a learner-preview check as Essentials requirements to test, not as something these products already prove.

references.title: Add sources picker for Dash chat
references.question: Q1
references.take: Dropbox Dash combines search or paste link, existing-source selection, and Upload in one 'Add sources' dialog for chat context.

references.title: Digital product content and insert tools
references.question: Q1
references.take: Gumroad's digital-product Content area places rich-text and link tools, a closed 'Insert' menu, and page creation together.

references.title: Adding a file from New lesson
references.question: Q1
references.take: Podia groups text, embed, quiz, coaching and file lesson types under one 'New lesson' menu in the course outline.

references.title: Instructor video setup without preview
references.question: Q1
references.take: Squarespace configures lesson video in an instructor dialog. It does not show preview or playback.

references.title: Course editor PDF upload area
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable's 'Add PDF' dialog brings together local upload, several cloud providers and URL input inside lesson editing.

references.title: File upload or URL redirect setup
references.question: Q1
references.take: A Teachable digital-product setup screen places 'File upload' and 'Redirect to URL' together, but it is not clearly course-lesson authoring.

references.title: Adding a PDF from Add content
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable separates content types in one 'Add content' list, then brings device, cloud and URL sources together in the PDF Viewer dialog. The screenshots include alternative source branches, not one required linear sequence.

references.title: Mobile lesson with media views
references.question: Q2
references.take: Coursera organises media and supporting views inside a sequential lesson shell on mobile.

references.title: Course as one freeform document
references.question: Q2
references.take: Gumroad can organise course content as one freeform document rather than folders, modules or lesson rows.

references.title: Adding a course module
references.question: Q2
references.take: Kajabi organises course content as modules with optional submodules and nested learning items.

references.title: Module copy with mixed linked resources
references.question: Q2
references.take: Podia embeds mixed links and files directly inside a module-based instructor editing screen.

references.title: Flat lesson list and resource tab
references.question: Q2
references.take: Skillshare presents learners with a flat ordered lesson sequence and puts resources in another tab.

references.title: Downloads grouped apart from videos
references.question: Q2
references.take: SuperHi groups learner materials by content type, separating downloads from numbered videos.

references.title: Curriculum with ordered section lessons
references.question: Q2
references.take: Teachable uses named course sections containing ordered lesson rows with a short content summary on each item.

references.title: Copy or move a design into a course
references.question: Q3
references.take: Canva lets an instructor choose an existing design from the central Projects hierarchy and explicitly copy it into or move it into the current course.

references.title: All files library with shared folders
references.question: Q3
references.take: Dropbox shows a lasting central All files area that mixes shared, team and other folders, but not reuse inside courses.

references.title: Inline course video with controls
references.question: Q4
references.take: Coursera embeds video playback and study tools inside the desktop lesson shell.

references.title: Mobile lesson with attachment tab
references.question: Q4
references.take: Coursera keeps mobile video and supporting lesson tabs in one sequential view.

references.title: View file from list to side preview
references.question: Q4
references.take: Dropbox Dash moves from an item list to a quick look to a side-pane preview, while keeping the library context.

references.title: Lesson video with downloads panel
references.question: Q4
references.take: Kajabi puts lesson media, outline, completion, text and a downloadable file on one learner page.

references.title: Mobile player with course files note
references.question: Q4
references.take: Skillshare keeps video playback and lesson download status in the lesson, but sends learners to another course tab for files.

references.title: Course content visibility screen
references.question: Q5
references.take: Kajabi makes a lesson's Draft or Published choice prominent beside its details.

references.title: Updating visibility from Hidden
references.question: Q5
references.take: Podia changes a lesson from 'Hidden' to visible through its row overflow menu, but does not leave a lasting visible label.

references.title: Setting status for a lesson
references.question: Q5
references.take: Squarespace shows lesson status in the course outline and supports Draft, Published or Scheduled with a date and time picker.

references.title: Course material status and drip
references.question: Q5
references.take: Teachable's curriculum screen pairs per-lesson 'Publish' buttons with a section-level drip panel offering days after enrollment or a specific date.

references.title: Adding a drip at section level
references.question: Q5
references.take: Teachable applies enrollment-relative drip at section level while keeping lesson publication as a separate row action.

references.title: Learner Resources beside course modules
references.question: Q6
references.take: Coursera shows a dedicated learner Resources branch beside Course Material modules. That suggests neighbouring structures rather than a proven mirror of the instructor editor.

references.title: Learner course resource view
references.question: Q6
references.take: Skillshare ties project resources to lesson progression by references, while placing downloads in a separate learner tab.

references.title: Instructor sections without learner pair
references.question: Q6
references.take: Teachable's instructor editor groups lessons into named sections and shows a DOCX resource beneath lesson text. A matching learner screen is not in these screenshots.

references.title: Learner player Downloads tab
references.question: Q6
references.take: Udemy shows learner access to lesson downloads, not how an instructor adds upload, link or embed material.
